title: Lower Doon zoning changes and deferred developments
subtitle: Fischer Hallman towers approved, lodging houses and 417 King West deferred, council budgets, sponsorship strategy, building by-law
overview: Council adopted the Lower Doon Land Use Study with changes. Mixed Use designation and zoning now apply to the vacant part of 2350-2440 Homer Watson Boulevard. The proposed higher-density RES-5 zoning was replaced with RES-4 on most properties, which limits stacked townhouses in the historic neighbourhood. The amendment passed {{vote:m4}}. Council also approved the Official Plan and zoning changes for two towers at 1198 Fischer Hallman Road {{vote:m1}}.

Two contentious files were put off. The city-wide lodging house review was referred to a standing committee so it can be considered with a new Lodging House Licensing By-law, expected in early 2024. The 55-storey proposal at 417 King Street West was deferred to December 11 so staff can talk with NAV Canada about airport runway approach impacts.

Council also set term budgets for councillors' home office, conference and community engagement costs, adopted a new minimum maintenance standard and a delegated weather-event declaration, updated the Building By-law, renewed the regional economic development partnership and endorsed a downtown vision. The Dangerous Dog Designation appeal decision was confirmed with modified conditions.

decisions.detail: Council adopted the Official Plan and zoning changes with amendments: Mixed Use for the vacant Homer Watson Boulevard lands, and RES-4 instead of RES-5 on most properties.
Council adopted the Official Plan amendment, to be sent to the Region for approval, and approved the zoning change for the Activa development.
The proposal to permit lodging houses city-wide was referred to a standing committee, to be considered with a new licensing by-law expected in Q1 2024.
The 55-storey mixed-use proposal was deferred to December 11, 2023 so staff can engage NAV Canada on airport runway approach impacts.
Council set term-limit funding envelopes for home office and technology, conferences and training, and community engagement, and repealed the separate technology and home office policy.
Council delegated authority to declare a significant weather event and adopted O. Reg. 239/02 as the minimum maintenance standards.
Council approved the amended sponsorship strategy and policy and asked staff to report back by the end of 2024.
Council endorsed the downtown vision and principles and directed staff to use them to develop an action plan.

debate: Delegates for property owners and a developer argued that RES-5 zoning would add housing, including student housing, near Conestoga College. They said it keeps site plan control, which RES-4 lacks. One planner said the change was too large to decide without more consultation.

Supporters of RES-4 said Lower Doon is the city's oldest area and residents accept growth but want it compatible with the neighbourhood's character. They noted that triplexes and fourplexes are already permitted and that large amounts of density are planned on the south side.

Staff said RES-4 stays within the low-rise Official Plan designation but that a council decision against the staff recommendation could be appealed. Council would then need its own planning expert, and the Ontario Land Tribunal has mostly favoured developers. Council briefly considered a closed session on this.

On Fischer Hallman, the applicant's planner kept the original tower design, citing separation from nearby homes and design proportions. A councillor asked for affordable housing or a community benefit in return for the added height, and for traffic review and public access to the amenity space through site plan.

On lodging houses, delegates said they are a necessary, relatively affordable housing option and warned against a pilot project. Councillors who backed the deferral said they support lodging houses but want the policy and licensing rules considered together.
